ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: In a large skillet, warm the mushroom broth over medium heat. Carefully lay the cod fillets in the pan, skin side down. Season each fillet lightly with salt and pepper. Spoon the ragout over the cod fillets, cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the fish is tender.
Use a spatula to carefully lift the mushroom-topped fish onto 4 individual plates. Divide the poaching broth over each fillet, garnish each with minced parsley and serve with boiled potatoes.

ingredients.raw: 6 tablespoons melted butter, plus additional butter for greasing the mold
ingredients.preparation: plus additional butter for greasing the mold

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Sift the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt into a bowl. Add the cornmeal and stir.
In a separate bowl, beat the eggs until foamy. Add the eggs to the dry mixture, along with the milk, vanilla and melted butter. Beat just until smooth (do not overmix).

Grease the mold well, and fill the mold cavities to seven-eighths of capacity with the batter. Bake for 20 minutes, or until the muffins are lightly browned. (The pan has ''feet,'' so it is helpful to set it on a cookie sheet in the oven to avoid tipping.)

ingredients.raw: Coarse salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: coarse salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

steps.text: Blanch the corn in salted water and drain. Seed and chop the peppers and tomatoes.
Combined the vegetables in a serving bowl and sprinkle with basil.
Mix the vinegar and oil and season to taste. Pour the mixture over the vegetables and toss.

name: Coconut Kitchri With Jammy Eggs
author: Zaynab Issa
description: Kitchri is a popular South Asian savory porridge made with rice and lentils. The flavor adaptations for it are endless, and this version looks to kuku paka, an East African coconut milk-based curry, for inspiration — featuring the same aromatic curry base, warming ground spices and coconut milk to form the broth in which the rice and lentils cook. Since kitchri always includes lentils, it’s already a complete meal, but serving it with jammy eggs adds even more protein and also nods to kuku paka, since boiled eggs are often served in the curry. To cut the richness of this kitchri, any crunchy, spicy vegetables or fresh herbs will pair well as a garnish, especially when finished with a drizzle of tangy, salty yogurt.

ingredients.raw: 1 serrano chile (optional), roughly chopped, deseeded if desired
1 (1-inch) piece fresh ginger, peeled and roughly chopped
1 tablespoon ghee, coconut oil or neutral-tasting oil
½ cup uncooked jasmine or basmati rice
Red onion, sliced into thin wedges

steps.text: Start the kitchri: In a food processor, blender or mini chopper, combine onion, tomato, chile, garlic and ginger and process until smooth.

Heat a medium pot over medium-high. Add ghee, and once melted, swirl the pot to coat the bottom. Add the onion mixture and season with 2 ½ teaspoons of salt. Cook, stirring often, until the water has evaporated and the mixture is paste-like, about 10 minutes.

Add a few grinds of black pepper, the cumin, coriander and turmeric, and stir to combine before stirring in the coconut milk. Add 5 cups of water (you can fill up the empty coconut milk can three times), stir to combine and bring to a boil over high heat.

Meanwhile, add lentils and rice to a fine-mesh strainer and rinse under cold running water until the water runs mostly clear. Once the coconut mixture is boiling, add the lentils and rice, stir to combine and reduce the heat to medium to maintain a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the lentils and rice have completely broken down and absorbed most of the liquid, about 25 minutes. The texture should be similar to loose oatmeal and will thicken slightly as it cools.
Meanwhile, stir ½ teaspoon of salt into the yogurt.
Serve bowls of kitchri, topped with soft-boiled egg halves, a drizzle of salted yogurt, more black pepper and your desired toppings.

name: Corn and Jalapeño Egg Bites
author: Ali Slagle
description: These altogether sweet, salty, spicy and silky egg bites are studded with corn, feta, scallions and jalapeño. They’re a riff on Naz Deravian’s recipe and not at all rubbery, thanks to cottage cheese and baking the eggs in a water bath in a low-temperature oven. You could improvise further by adding cooked bacon, or swapping the feta for shredded Cheddar. The egg bites will keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days and in the freezer for up to 3 months. Reheat in a microwave or a 300-degree oven until warmed through.

ingredients.raw: 1 cup (8 ounces) full-fat cottage cheese (or whole milk)
ingredients.item: (8 ounces) full-fat cottage cheese (or whole milk)

ingredients.raw: ¾ cup corn kernels (fresh, canned or frozen and unthawed)

steps.text: Heat the oven to 325 degrees. In a tea kettle or a medium saucepan, bring 3 cups of water to a boil. Coat 12 standard muffin cups generously with nonstick spray and place on a sheet pan.

In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, cottage cheese and salt until homogenous. Pour the egg mixture into the muffin cups until three-quarters of the way full (about ¼ cup). Top with the corn, feta, scallions and jalapeño.

Place the sheet pan on the oven rack, then carefully pour the hot water into the sheet pan. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until set. Remove the muffin pan from the sheet pan and set aside for 5 minutes, then run a knife or offset spatula around the edges of the egg bites and lift them out of the pan. (Let the sheet pan cool in the oven before disposing of the remaining water.)

name: Herby Cottage Cheese Egg Bake
author: Yossy Arefi
description: This unassuming baked egg dish is packed with flavor and can be prepped the night before you plan to bake it. Using a blend of herbs often used in kuku sabzi gives it a bright flavor and color that develops even more after an overnight rest. A generous amount of cottage cheese and mozzarella adds richness (and protein). Slice it into squares and serve with a salad or sandwich it in between a pita or other soft bread. A food processor works well to chop the herbs, but the scallions can get a bit slimy so it’s best to chop those by hand. This can also be prepped and made the day you serve it, no rest required. A garnish of fresh chopped herbs and feta make it even better.

ingredients.raw: 1 ½ cups/60 grams finely chopped soft herbs, such as dill, parsley and cilantro (a combination of least two types of herbs works best), loosely packed, plus more for garnish
ingredients.item: cups/60 grams finely chopped soft herbs
ingredients.preparation: such as dill, parsley and cilantro (a combination of least two types of herbs works best), loosely packed, plus more for garnish

ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)

steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until homogenous. Add the cottage cheese, 1½ cups chopped herbs, scallions, salt and pepper and stir gently to combine. If desired, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Heat oven to 375 degrees and butter a 9-by-13-inch baking dish.

Stir the egg mixture briefly and pour into the prepared pan. Sprinkle the mozzarella cheese over the top and bake until just set in the middle, 25 to 30 minutes. If desired, briefly broil the egg bake to brown the cheese topping. If desired, finish with a sprinkle of feta and more herbs. Cut into squares and serve warm, at room temperature or cold.

name: Coconut Rice And Quinoa
author: Ali Slagle
description: This pot of grains is rich, sweet, nutty and full of textures. Start by toasting coconut flakes with raw quinoa for an optional crisp topping, then steam rice and more quinoa with coconut milk. The floral quality of the coconut tempers any bitterness of the quinoa, and cooking rice and quinoa together makes a fluffy, light combination. Serve this as a side to laab, tofu or dal; or make it a meal with a fried egg, lime, and hot sauce.

ingredients.raw: 1 cup unsweetened coconut flakes or shredded coconut (optional)
ingredients.item: unsweetened coconut flakes or shredded coconut

ingredients.raw: 1 cup long-grain white rice, such as jasmine or basmati

steps.text: If you’re making the coconut-flake topping: Heat the coconut flakes and 1 tablespoon quinoa in a large pot over medium. Stir until the coconut is golden and the quinoa makes a popping sound, 3 to 6 minutes. Pour into a bowl. (Don’t worry about getting out every little bit.)

To the pot, add the remaining quinoa, rice, coconut milk and 1 teaspoon salt. Fill the coconut can up with water and add that to the pot. Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low and cook until the grains are tender and a thin white tail appears on the quinoa, 17 to 20 minutes. Turn off the heat and let rest for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork, season to taste with salt, and sprinkle with the toasted coconut and quinoa.

name: Coconut and Mango Layer Cake
author: Yewande Komolafe
description: All year round, coconut inspires the chef Dria Atencio of Salty Lunch Lady’s Little Luncheonette in Ridgewood, Queens. Her summer menu, in particular, features a coconut-mango cake, tender and white with bright yellow layers of what she affectionately calls “mango party,” a mix of mango curd and jam. Her intent is to incorporate coconut into every bite, so she folds sweetened flakes into the batter. A fluffy cream cheese frosting, complete with an angelic shower of coconut flakes, surrounds the cake. This recipe follows her method with a slight tweak: The cake is made to fit three pans instead of four, and frozen mangoes can be used instead of fresh. Both cake and mango party can be made ahead of time, cooled, wrapped and stored in the refrigerator until ready to assemble. Take care to refrigerate while assembling to keep the layers from sliding. A show-stopping dessert, this cake is as delicious as it looks, with every forkful a moment to pause and celebrate.

ingredients.raw: 1 cup/227 grams unsalted butter, at room temperature, plus 1 tablespoon melted butter for the pans
ingredients.preparation: at room temperature, plus 1 tablespoon melted butter for the pans

ingredients.raw: 2½ cups/335 grams all-purpose flour, plus more for the pans
2 teaspoons kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)
½ cup/140 grams sweetened condensed coconut milk
ingredients.item: cup/140 grams sweetened condensed coconut milk

ingredients.raw: 6 large egg whites, at room temperature (reserve the yolks for the mango curd filling)
ingredients.preparation: at room temperature (reserve the yolks for the mango curd filling)

ingredients.raw: 1 cup/90 grams tightly packed sweetened shredded coconut
ingredients.item: cup/90 grams tightly packed sweetened shredded coconut

ingredients.raw: 2 cups/454 grams fresh or frozen (thawed) peeled mango chunks
ingredients.item: cups/454 grams fresh or frozen (thawed) peeled mango chunks

ingredients.raw: Grated zest from 2 medium limes (zested limes reserved for Mango Curd)
ingredients.item: grated zest from 2 medium limes (zested limes reserved for mango curd)

ingredients.raw: 1 (1-inch) piece fresh ginger, scrubbed and grated (about 1 ½ teaspoons grated)
ingredients.preparation: scrubbed and grated (about 1 ½ teaspoons grated)

ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)
½ cup/131 grams canned mango purée or pulp, or frozen mango pulp (thawed)
ingredients.item: cup/131 grams canned mango purée or pulp

ingredients.raw: ½ cup/120 milliliters lime juice (from 3 to 4 medium limes)
ingredients.item: cup/120 milliliters lime juice (from 3 to 4 medium limes)

ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)
6 egg yolks, reserved from making cake
1 cup/227 grams unsalted butter, cut into 1-inch pieces, at room temperature
ingredients.preparation: cut into 1-inch pieces, at room temperature

ingredients.raw: 1 ½ teaspoons kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)
8 ounces/226 grams cream cheese, cut into 2-inch pieces, at room temperature
ingredients.preparation: cut into 2-inch pieces, at room temperature

ingredients.raw: 1 ½ cups/130 grams sweetened shredded coconut

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350 degrees and arrange racks in the upper half and lower third of the oven. Cut 3 (9-inch) parchment circles and line 3 (9-inch) round cake pans with them. Brush parchment and sides with 1 tablespoon melted butter and sprinkle with flour; set aside.
In a medium bowl, combine 2½ cups/335 grams flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Set aside.

In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, mix 1 cup/227 grams butter, sugar and condensed coconut milk until fluffy, about 5 minutes. Scrape down the bottom and sides of the bowl. Add egg whites, vanilla and coconut extract (if using), and mix until just combined, about 1 minute.

Add half the dry ingredients. Using a flexible spatula, fold until just combined. Add buttermilk, remaining dry ingredients and shredded coconut. Fold gently until just blended (a few remaining streaks of buttermilk are OK). Divide the batter among the prepared pans (about 475 grams per pan) and spread evenly with a spatula.

Transfer cake pans to oven, arranging two pans on the lower rack and one on the upper rack. Bake, rotating each pan and swapping rack positions halfway through, until the cake edges are golden brown and the surface is pale and springy to the touch, 35 to 40 minutes. Cool cake in the pans for 10 minutes, then loosen each cake from pan, invert and peel off the parchment and move to a rack to cool completely. (When wrapped tightly in plastic, the cakes can be refrigerated for up to 1 day or frozen for up to 2 weeks.)

Combine mango chunks, sugar, lime zest and juice, water, grated ginger, vanilla and salt in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Bring to a vigorous simmer, stirring occasionally, and cook until the mango becomes translucent and its juices are thick and jammy, 10 minutes. Transfer to a medium bowl and let cool to room temperature.

Set a fine-mesh sieve over a clean small mixing bowl and place next to the stove. In a medium saucepan, combine the mango purée, lime juice, sugar, butter and salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until mixture just begins to simmer, bubbling at the edges, 6 to 8 minutes. Turn heat to low.

In a second small bowl, briefly whisk the egg yolks to break them up. Slowly whisk in ½ cup of the hot mango mixture into eggs to temper. Slowly pour tempered egg mixture back into the saucepan, then cook, whisking constantly, until the curd thickens enough to coat a spatula, about 5 minutes. Strain through the fine-mesh sieve into the clean small bowl. (You should have about 1½ cups/405 grams of curd.)
With an immersion blender, food processor or blender, purée the cooled mango jam until smooth. Mix in the mango curd. Cover and refrigerate until ready to use. (This is your Mango Party.)

To the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the (cleaned) paddle attachment, add powdered sugar, butter, salt, vanilla extract and coconut extract (if using). Mix on medium-high until creamy and lighter in color, 4 minutes. Scrape down bottom and sides of the bowl. With the mixer on medium-high, gradually mix in cream cheese, a piece at a time. Scrape down bottom and sides, and beat on high speed until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. With a flexible spatula, scrape down the bowl again and stir briefly to ensure the frosting is smooth. (You should have about 4 cups frosting.)

To assemble, spread a small spoonful of frosting onto a cake round or serving plate to hold the cake in place. Place the first layer of cake, top side down. Spread about 1 cup frosting on top of the cake, pushing frosting toward the sides to form a thicker “rim” around the edge. Dollop about ½ cup Mango Party onto the frosting and spread in the center, leaving a 2-inch gap between the edge of the Mango Party and the frosting so it doesn't spill out the sides when the cake is assembled.

Place the second cake layer on top, top side down, and repeat with another 1 cup frosting and ½ cup Mango Party. Transfer the unfinished cake to the refrigerator and chill briefly to keep the layers from sliding, 10 minutes. Place the final cake layer on top of the stack, top side down, and spread the top and sides of the layer cake with a thin, even layer of frosting, leaving some frosting for the next step. Refrigerate the cake until the frosting is firm, about 30 minutes. (Refrigerate any remaining Mango Party for another use.)

Spread remaining buttercream evenly over the cake and sprinkle the top and sides with shredded coconut. Cut in wedges and serve. (The fully assembled cake can be stored, loosely covered and refrigerated, for up to 3 days. Remove the cake from the refrigerator to come back to room temperature before serving.)
